title: Measuring Tabular Data Formats Cold: A Replicated Cold-Cache Benchmark of Serialization, Scan, and Index Performance on Real Datasets
abstract: arXiv:2611.10398v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Choosing a file format for tabular data is a routine engineering decision, yet published comparisons often time reads served from the operating-system page cache, use one session, or rely on a single synthetic dataset. This article benchmarks fifteen format and access-path configurations (CSV, JSON Lines, Pickle, Feather, Parquet, ORC, DuckDB, and SQLite, with several access paths) on two real public datasets, New York City taxi trips and United States airline on-time records, at 50,000 to 3 million rows. Every measurement uses an explicitly cold cache, randomized execution order, and three independent sessions (with restarts on the laptop), and is analyzed with bootstrap intervals and Holm-adjusted permutation tests. Parquet answered a filtered aggregation 2.6 to 11 times faster than CSV, while JSON Lines was 10 to 27 times slower. translated_title: 冷缓存下的表格数据格式基准测量：基于真实数据集的序列化、扫描与索引性能的复现实验
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.10398v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：为表格数据选择文件格式是一项日常的工程决策，但已发表的比较结果往往是在操作系统页面缓存预热的情况下进行读取计时、使用单次会话，或仅依赖单一的合成数据集。本文对十五种文件格式与访问路径配置（CSV、JSON Lines、Pickle、Feather、Parquet、ORC、DuckDB 和 SQLite，包含多种访问路径）进行了基准测试，使用了两个真实的公开数据集，即纽约市出租车行程数据和美国航班准点率数据，数据规模从 5 万行到 300 万行。每次测量均显式使用冷缓存、随机化的执行顺序以及三次独立会话（在笔记本电脑上伴随重启），并采用自助法置信区间和经 Holm 校正的置换检验进行分析。结果显示，Parquet 在过滤聚合查询上的速度比 CSV 快 2.6 到 11 倍，而 JSON Lines 则慢 10 到 27 倍。二级索引在随机顺序的数据上使 SQLite 查询慢了 2.6 到 4.8 倍，并...
tldr: 该论文在真实数据集上采用显式冷缓存、随机化执行顺序和多会话的严格基准测试方法，系统比较了十五种表格数据格式的性能，发现 Parquet 比显著快于 CSV 和 JSON Lines，而二级索引在某些数据布局下反而会拖慢 SQLite 查询。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a rigorous cold-cache, randomized-order, multi-session benchmark of fifteen tabular data format configurations on real public datasets, showing that Parquet is 2.6-11x faster than CSV for filtered aggregations while JSON Lines is 10-27x slower, and that a secondary index can even slow down SQLite queries on randomly ordered data.
